newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Dounreay nuclear workers lobby watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Dounreay nuclear workers lobby watchdog.

text.p: Workers at Scotland's Dounreay nuclear reprocessing plant have lobbied a government watchdog in an effort to prevent the introduction of tough measures on foreign waste recycling that they claim could cost jobs.
Dounreay contracts include controversial deals to import highly radioactive fuel rods from foreign plants for recycling.

The workers have sent a petition to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA) claiming that recycling work has been carried out safely for over 30 years and the plant is safe. The SEPA meets on Tuesday to discuss an application from the Atomic Energy Authority (AEA) for new consents to discharge radioactive liquids into the sea and gases into the air as a result of recycling.
The agency has signalled a tough stance over radioactive discharges and some members question Dounreay's foreign recycling contracts, wanting these wastes to be returned immediately.

Although there have been "return to sender" clauses in all Dounreay waste recycling deals signed since 1990, these envisage "hot" wastes being stored at Dounreay for up to 25 years before being shipped back abroad.
If the SEPA backs draconian moves, the foreign contracts could end, the workers argued, with the possible loss of 30 jobs and a knock-on effect over the plant as a whole.

Dounreay's reprocessing activities include recovering enriched uranium from specialist fuel rods burned in the cores of non-power reactors to produce radioactive isotope sources for cancer treatments and industrial uses.
